About the Academy

An approach built on trust, not pressure

At Paws and Progress Academy, training is treated as a conversation between you and your dog — unhurried, observant and always kind.

Rather than rushing towards results, the academy focuses on understanding how each dog learns: what motivates them, what worries them, and what helps them feel safe enough to try something new. Sessions are structured around clear, achievable steps, so progress feels steady and rewarding for both ends of the lead.

Owners are part of the learning, too. You will be shown how to read your dog's body language, reward the behaviour you want to see more of, and practise calmly at home — turning everyday moments into quiet opportunities to learn together.

  • 01Observe firstEvery programme begins by understanding your dog as an individual.
  • 02Small, clear stepsSkills are built gradually, at a pace your dog can succeed at.
  • 03Learn togetherOwners are coached alongside their dogs, so learning continues at home.

Why Us

Why families choose the academy approach

Four simple commitments shape every session — whatever programme you and your dog are following.

Positive training

Learning is reward-based and force-free in spirit — dogs are encouraged, never intimidated, so they offer behaviour willingly.

Small groups

Sessions are kept small in design, so each dog and owner can be seen, heard and guided individually.

Progress tracking

Each step is broken down and noted as you go, so you can see how far you and your dog have come.

Care at the centre

Your dog's comfort comes first — rest, water and time to settle are treated as part of the lesson, not an afterthought.

Begin with a conversation — not a commitment.

Tell us a little about your dog, and what you would love training to feel like.
